learn: Composers create music by choosing pitches, rhythms, harmonies, timbres and form.
Composing is a process: idea, sketch, develop, revise, finish.
Many composers start with a short motif.
lessons.try: Write three different four-note motifs.

learn: Compose on paper or with free notation software like MuseScore.
Digital audio workstations (DAWs) record and arrange sound.
Save versions often.
lessons.try: Notate your motifs in MuseScore.

learn: Listen for how composers build and release tension.
Note techniques you'd like to borrow.
Compare different settings of the same idea.
lessons.try: Analyse how one piece builds tension.

learn: Major: W W H W W W H. Natural minor: W H W W H W W.
Relative keys share a key signature: C major and A minor.
Harmonic minor raises the seventh.
check: The relative minor of C major is...
lessons.try: Write G major and E minor scales.

learn: Intervals measure distance: seconds, thirds, fourths, fifths, sixths, sevenths, octaves.
Qualities: major, minor, perfect, augmented, diminished.
Consonant intervals sound stable; dissonant ones create tension.
check: C to G is a perfect...
C to E is a major...
lessons.try: Sing or play each interval and name it.

learn: The circle of fifths arranges keys by adding one sharp or flat at a time.
Neighbouring keys sound closely related.
It helps with modulation and key signatures.
lessons.try: Draw and label the circle of fifths.

learn: Contour is a melody's shape: arch, wave, rising, falling.
Singable melodies stay within about an octave and move mostly by step.
A climax is the melody's high point.
lessons.try: Write an eight-bar melody with a clear climax.

learn: Phrases are musical sentences, often four bars.
Antecedent (question) and consequent (answer) phrases form a period.
Repeat, sequence and vary motifs for unity.
check: A sequence repeats a motif at a different...
lessons.try: Write a question-and-answer phrase pair.

learn: Pentatonic melodies sound open and folk-like.
Modes (Dorian, Mixolydian) give different moods.
Blue notes add expressive colour.
lessons.try: Write the same melody in major, minor and Dorian.

learn: A triad stacks two thirds: root, third, fifth.
Major, minor, diminished and augmented triads.
In a major key, I, IV, V are major; ii, iii, vi minor; vii° diminished.
check: In a major key, ii is...
lessons.try: Build all seven triads in C major.

learn: Seventh chords add a fourth note: the dominant seventh (V7) pulls strongly to I.
Inversions put a different chord tone in the bass.
Inversions create smooth bass lines.
lessons.try: Play a chord progression using inversions.

learn: Move each voice by the smallest step possible.
Keep common tones between chords.
Avoid parallel fifths and octaves in traditional style.
lessons.try: Harmonise a melody in four parts.

learn: I-IV-V-I is the foundation of much Western music.
I-V-vi-IV appears in many pop songs.
ii-V-I is central to jazz.
lessons.try: Write a melody over I-V-vi-IV.

learn: Authentic (V-I) sounds final; half (ending on V) sounds unfinished.
Plagal (IV-I) is the "Amen" cadence; deceptive (V-vi) surprises.
Cadences punctuate phrases.
lessons.try: Identify cadences in a hymn or folk song.

learn: Modulation moves to a new key.
Pivot chords belong to both keys.
Pop songs often lift up a step for the final chorus.
check: Pop songs often lift ___ for the last chorus.
lessons.try: Modulate a short piece from C to G using a pivot chord.

learn: Simple metres divide beats into two; compound metres into three (6/8).
Syncopation accents off-beats.
Changing metres create surprise.
lessons.try: Compose a rhythm in 6/8 with syncopation.

learn: A groove is a repeating rhythmic feel that makes people move.
An ostinato is a repeated pattern.
Bass and drums lock together in many grooves.
lessons.try: Create a two-bar drum groove and a bass ostinato.

learn: Polyrhythm layers different divisions (3 against 2).
Tempo affects mood: slow (largo), fast (allegro, presto).
Rubato flexes tempo expressively.
lessons.try: Clap a 3-against-2 polyrhythm with a partner.

learn: Verse-chorus is common in popular music.
AABA (32-bar form) appears in jazz standards.
A bridge provides contrast.
lessons.try: Map the form of three favourite songs.

learn: Binary (AB), ternary (ABA), rondo (ABACA), theme and variations, sonata form.
Repetition creates unity; contrast creates interest.
Form helps listeners follow the music.
lessons.try: Compose a short piece in ternary form.

learn: Develop ideas by inversion, retrograde, augmentation, diminution and fragmentation.
Augmentation lengthens note values; diminution shortens them.
Fragmentation uses part of a motif.
lessons.try: Develop a motif using four techniques.

learn: Each instrument has a comfortable range.
Transposing instruments (clarinet, trumpet, horn) sound different from written pitch.
Check ranges before writing.
check: Writing outside the range makes parts...
lessons.try: Make a range chart for five instruments.

learn: Combine timbres for colour: doubling, layering, contrast.
Balance: brass can overpower strings and woodwinds.
Leave space; not everyone plays all the time.
lessons.try: Orchestrate a melody for a small ensemble.

learn: SATB: soprano, alto, tenor, bass.
Keep vocal lines singable with breathing places.
Set syllables clearly.
check: SATB stands for soprano, alto, tenor and...
lessons.try: Write a four-bar SATB passage.

learn: Put stressed syllables on strong beats.
Match melody shape to the meaning of words.
Public domain poems are free to set.
lessons.try: Set a public domain poem by Emily Dickinson or Christina Rossetti.

learn: Word painting illustrates words: rising on "heaven", falling on "down".
Harmony and tempo can reflect mood.
Repetition emphasises key lines.
lessons.try: Add word painting to your setting.

learn: Hooks are memorable phrases.
Lyrics need rhyme, rhythm and a clear idea.
Co-writing shares ideas and credits.
check: Songs often include a verse, chorus and...
lessons.try: Write an original song with verse, chorus and bridge.

learn: Add dynamics, articulations, tempo and expression marks.
Check for errors and readable layout.
Prepare parts for each performer.
lessons.try: Produce a clean score and parts.

learn: Rehearse with performers and revise based on feedback.
Record with good microphone placement.
Mix levels so all parts are heard.
lessons.try: Record a performance of your piece.

learn: Share via concerts, online platforms or competitions.
You own the copyright to your original music.
Choose a licence (for example Creative Commons) if you want others to reuse it.
check: A Creative Commons licence lets others...
lessons.try: Write programme notes and share your piece.
